Counsel for Opposite Party :- Akash Misra,G.A.,Santosh Singh
Hon'ble Subhash Chandra Sharma,J.
Counter affidavit filed by learned counsel for the opposite party today is taken on record.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned counsel for the respondent alongwith learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.

The present transfer application has been moved with prayer to transfer the Case No.79 of 2022 (Pallavi Tyagi vs. Shubham Tyagi) under Section 12 Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005, Police Station Murad Nagar, District Ghaziabad pending in the court of Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate IV, Ghaziabad, from District Court Ghaziabad to the competent court at District Mathura.

sentences.text:
It is submitted that a case u/s 12 Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 was filed in Ghaziabad by the applicant which is pending the court of Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate IV,
Ghaziabad.

entities.text: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
entities.label: STATUTE

entities.text:
Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate IV,
Ghaziabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Further submitted that applicant is wedded wife of opposite party no.2, opposite party no.3 is her mother-in-law, opposite party no.4 & 5 are married nanad & nandoi who all are living at Ghaziabad.
When the complaint was filed in Ghaziabad by the applicant, she was living at Delhi with her grand parents.
Now her grand mother has started living at Mathura, therefore, she has also come to live with her grand mother at Mahtura.
The distance between Mathura and Ghaziabad is more than 150 Kms.

that is the reason she is not in a position to attend the court proceedings from Ghaziabad to Mathura, therefore, request the transfer the case from the court at Ghaziabad to the competent court at Mathura.

Learned counsel for the opposite party opposed the prayer as aforesaid and contended that in addition to the present complaint, case u/s 498A I.P.C. and other case u/s 13 Hindu Marriage Act have also been filed by the applicant at Ghaziabad against the opposite parties who are husband,
mother-in-law, nanad and nandoi.
The present transfer application has been moved only for the purpose of harassment of the opposite parties those are all family members of the husband.

In case,
the case is transferred from Ghaziabad to Mathura, it will cause grave inconvenience to the opposite parties including old mother-in-law and married nanad.
There is no any other reason to get the case transferred from Ghaziabad to Mathura.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties as well as learned A.G.A., perusal of record, the convenience to the applicant and the opposite parties, there appears no any sufficient ground to transfer the case from Ghaziabad to Mathura.
Accordingly, this transfer application is, hereby, rejected.

Order Date :- 15.5.2024 Ashok Gupta  Pallavi Tyagi vs State Of Up And 4 Others on 15 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/6425812/
